correctness.rationale: For n>=3, dominating subsets of Cr_n are exactly whole shores, selections of at least two from both shores, or singleton in one shore together with its matched partner in the other and at least one further opposite vertex. These disjoint cases give D_n(z)=2z^n+((1+z)^n-1-nz)^2+n z²(2(1+z)^(n-1)-1). Crown distances are 1 across nonmatched sides, 2 within a side and 3 only for matched opposite pairs. Removing these disjoint forbidden pairs from the complete partner graph still permits a perfect matching for any even chosen set size>=4. The only size-2 dominating subsets are matched pairs and cannot partner. Therefore P_pr2=(D_n(z)+D_n(-z))/2 - n z²; minimum 4 with coefficient C(n,2)^2+2nC(n-1,2)+2*[n=4]. Independent literal matching enumeration and complete histograms for n3..6 agree.
